classification.difficultyReason: Use two reduced water depths in a trapezoidal side area, convert cubic metres to litres, then recognise a shallow rectangular lost layer.

content.prompt: A swimming pool is in the shape of a trapezoidal prism, as shown. The pool is 10 m long, 5 m wide, 1 m deep at one end and 2 m deep at the other end. The pool is filled with water until it is 10 cm from the top.

spec.description: Source pool wireframe, level top and vertical end walls, shallow endleft/deep right, sloped floor. Physical side cross-section length10/depths1and2, width5 in text only. No waterline or numerical dimension labels invented; top rim remains solid, rear hidden edges derived from actual view.
spec.answerVisibility: Original given measures only, no computed answer labels.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Calculate, to the nearest litre, the volume of water in the pool.

answer.worked:
The water depths are 0.9 m and 1.9 m. The water has a trapezoidal side cross-section.
$$\begin{aligned}V&=\tfrac12(0.9+1.9)(10)(5)=70\text{ m}^3\\V&=70000\text{ L}.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: After a group of children played in the pool, the level of the water is 0.15 m below the top. How much water, correct to the nearest litre, splashed out of the pool?

answer.worked:
The level drops from 0.10 m to 0.15 m below the top, a fall of 0.05 m. The lost layer covers the full rectangular water surface.
$$\begin{aligned}V_{\text{lost}}&=10(5)(0.05)=2.5\text{ m}^3\\V_{\text{lost}}&=2500\text{ L}.\end{aligned}$$
